title: XRootD Collector Health
description: Health of the xrdmoncollect pipeline itself: ingest and decode rates, packet loss, the reporting server fleet, correlation state, sink delivery and the shovel transport. Storage activity lives in the companion dashboard (grafana-cluster-dashboard.json).

panels.title: Collectors
panels.description: Collector processes answering the scrape.

panels.title: Servers reporting
panels.description: XRootD servers currently feeding this collector.

panels.title: Packets/s
panels.description: Monitor packets ingested per second.

panels.title: Documents/s
panels.description: Documents handed to the sinks, after filtering.

panels.title: Packet loss
panels.description: Datagrams missing from the pseq sequence, as a share of those received. Sustained loss means the kernel receive buffer or the network is dropping monitor traffic.

panels.title: Malformed/s
panels.description: Structurally invalid packets per second; should be zero.

panels.title: Correlation state
panels.description: Resident bytes held in the correlation dictionaries; bounded by --max-memory.

panels.title: Recv queue
panels.description: Packet batches waiting for the serializer. Sustained non-zero means the decoder is behind the receiver.

panels.title: Ingest funnel
panels.description: What arrives against what leaves. Packets received and documents emitted are the two ends; malformed, unknown-stream, filtered and estimated-lost account for what does not make it through. Filtered documents were dropped deliberately by a [filter] rule, so they are not a fault.

panels.title: Packets/s by stream
panels.description: Which monitoring streams the servers are actually sending. A stream that is flat at zero is one the servers were never configured to emit (xrootd.monitor ... flush/fstat/redir/...). g:<provider> entries are g-stream records broken out by the plugin that produced them.

panels.title: Records decoded by stream
panels.description: Per-stream decode rate once the packet has been unpacked into records.

panels.title: Malformed by reason
panels.description: Why packets failed to decode. truncated_string and short_packet point at an MTU or fbsz mismatch; bad_plen and trailing_bytes at a version skew or stray traffic on the port.

panels.title: Packet loss % by server
panels.description: Estimated from gaps in each stream's pseq counter, so it isolates the server whose datagrams are being dropped.

panels.title: Packets by server and stream
panels.description: One row per reporting server, one column per stream code, totalled over the dashboard window. A server with traffic but a zero f column is not sending fstat records, so none of its transfers will ever be correlated -- check its xrootd.monitor directive.

panels.title: Server inventory
panels.description: Every live server incarnation with the identity it advertised in its '=' ident record, plus what it sent over the dashboard window. Retired incarnations are excluded (server_info parks them at 0 rather than deleting them). The version column is the quickest way to find nodes still running an old XRootD.

panels.title: Servers reporting
panels.description: Live servers per storage cluster. A step down means nodes stopped reporting; a cluster named 'unknown' means a server has no all.sitename or has not sent its hourly ident record yet.

panels.title: Correlation state (bytes)
panels.description: Memory held by the correlation dictionaries; bounded by --max-memory.

panels.title: Evictions & reaps
panels.description: State turnover. Evictions mean the memory budget is being hit and correlations are being lost; reaps are idle server incarnations released by --server-ttl and are normal.

panels.title: Receive queue depth
panels.description: Sustained non-zero means the serializer is not keeping up with the receive loop; raise --queue-depth or reduce the document streams.

panels.title: Unpaired opens and closes
panels.description: Correlation failures. Stale opens are open records that never saw a close before the file TTL expired; orphan closes are closes whose open was lost or evicted. Both mean transfer documents are incomplete.

panels.title: Sink POST failures/s
panels.description: POSTs that failed after retries, per sink.

panels.title: Dropped bodies/s
panels.description: Bodies discarded after a failed POST with no disk cache, or with a cache that could not be written. This is data loss.

panels.title: Sink queue depth
panels.description: Bodies queued to the output thread; a growing backlog means the sink is slower than the collector.

panels.title: Disk cache backlog (files)
panels.description: On-failure cache depth; it drains oldest-first once the sink recovers.

panels.title: Disk cache backlog (bytes)
panels.description: The same backlog by size, which is what fills the state directory.

panels.title: Cache stored vs replayed/s
panels.description: Store rate rises during a backend outage; replay rate during recovery. Replay lagging store for long means the backlog is still growing.

panels.title: Shovel connections (collector)
panels.description: The collector's TCP listener. Auth failures mean a shared-secret mismatch; malformed means a protocol violation or a hello timeout.

panels.title: Shoveled datagrams/s
panels.description: Datagrams entering the collector over TCP against those the shovelers report having sent. A persistent gap means a shoveler cannot reach this collector. The shoveler series are not filtered by $collector -- they come from separate processes with their own instance labels.

panels.title: Shovel TCP throughput
panels.description: Bytes received on the collector's shovel connections.

panels.title: Shoveler pipeline/s
panels.description: Each shoveler's datagram flow: received over UDP, relayed live, spooled to disk while the collector was unreachable, and dropped outright because there was no usable spool.

panels.title: Shoveler spool backlog
panels.description: On-disk spool per shoveler. It grows during a collector outage and drains oldest-first on reconnect; sustained growth toward --spool-max means evictions, and evictions are lost data.

panels.title: Shoveler spool turnover/s
panels.description: Buffers written to and replayed from the spool, and the evictions forced by --spool-max. Any eviction rate above zero is data loss.

panels.title: Shoveler connectivity
panels.description: Per-shoveler connection state (1 = connected) and the connect rate, which is reconnect churn when it is not flat.

panels.title: Shoveler queues
panels.description: Batches queued from each shoveler's receiver to its sender, and the number of spooled buffers awaiting replay.
